CheckTitle: Explicit user assignment prevents unauthorized sign-in to non-Microsoft enterprise applications
Description: Non-Microsoft enterprise applications (service principals of type Application or Legacy) are evaluated for the **appRoleAssignmentRequired** property. When set to `true`, only users and groups explicitly assigned under "Users and groups" can obtain tokens for the application. When `false`, any tenant user including guests can sign in.
Risk: With **appRoleAssignmentRequired** set to `false`, every user in the directory — including guests — can sign in to the application and exercise whatever delegated permissions were admin-consented. A single compromised account can access every such app, widening the blast radius of an account takeover and enabling data exfiltration through third-party SaaS integrations.

Code.Other:
1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center (https://entra.microsoft.com)
2. Go to Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications
3. Select the application
4. Under Users and groups, assign the users or groups that need access
5. Go to Properties and set "Assignment required?" to **Yes**
6. Click Save

Recommendation.Text: Require **explicit assignment** on every non-Microsoft enterprise application to enforce **least privilege**. Before enabling, review the app's sign-in logs to identify users who need access, then assign them under "Users and groups" to avoid disruption.

Notes: Apps that only use application permissions (daemons) with no interactive sign-in will also FAIL when assignment is not required. Setting assignment required on them is harmless, so they are not excluded. Disabled service principals receive a PASS with an advisory message. Microsoft first-party apps are excluded and handled by a separate check.
